title: Is Arch Manning ready for Ohio State? Texas QB sharp in big win over Texas State
content:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning matched a career high with four touchdown passes in a 59-7 win over Texas State on Saturday in what served as a stress-free tuneup for the Longhorns’ Week 2 showdown with Ohio State.

Manning was sharp for the majority of the day, completing 20 of 27 pass attempts for 305 yards with one interception. He left the game midway through the third quarter with Texas leading Texas State 42-7.

The No. 5 Longhorns, who introduced a slew of high-impact transfers, had few issues with the overmatched Bobcats. Former Auburn receiver Cam Coleman, the No. 1 player in the transfer portal this offseason, caught Manning’s first touchdown pass, an easy 6-yard toss to a wide-open Coleman in the corner of the end zone.

Manning didn’t have to shoulder a ton of the load thanks to a strong running game, powered by transfer running backs Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown, who combined for 143 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns. The Texas defense also chipped in with three takeaways, one of which was a 59-yard fumble return by defensive back Graceson Littleton to give Texas a 28-0 second-quarter lead.

It marked a much better start to the season than Manning’s 2025 debut, when he struggled in a road loss to Ohio State and looked inconsistent throughout September. Manning was much more efficient and showed improved accuracy, particularly in the short and intermediate range, areas that were an issue at times last season. Manning went 16-for-22 passing for 179 yards on throws inside of 15 yards and completed 4 of 5 attempts for 126 yards on throws beyond 15 yards.

His lone interception came late in the first half. Manning forced a ball into coverage, and it was picked off by Texas State safety Ryan Nolan on third-and-11 with 11 seconds left in the second quarter. But Manning rebounded on his next opportunity, leading a six-play, 75-yard scoring drive to start the third quarter, capped by a 20-yard touchdown pass to Coleman. Manning looked Nolan off long enough to create a throwing window and hit Coleman despite getting hit just as he threw.

Ryan Wingo led all receivers with seven catches for 121 yards and a touchdown.

The true test for Manning comes next week, when the No. 1 Buckeyes roll into town. Ohio State rolled to a 56-3 home win over Ball State on Saturday. The Buckeyes won a defensive struggle over the Longhorns 14-7 last year in Columbus.

Though next week’s showdown against Ohio State will mean exponentially more to Manning’s NFL evaluation, it was still important for him to start the 2026 campaign on the right foot. He appeared to pick up where he left off last season, showing his trademark poise and toughness, and he made several key throws that resulted in big plays.

Manning also didn’t take long to lean on the upgraded talent around him, including his pair of touchdown tosses to Coleman, who joined Manning as a top-five prospect on my preseason draft board.

It wasn’t a perfect outing — before halftime, Manning didn’t account for the backside safety on a stick-nod concept, resulting in a red zone interception. But it was a minor blip in an otherwise sterling outing, a week before NFL scouts (and the Buckeyes) descend upon Austin. — Dane Brugler
